column2: Meaning
An informal ‘thanks’. Derived from ancient elven.
No literal translation: a being that is evil or a person with evil intent; used where ‘dark spawn’ would be.
Insult for a non-dark elf who pursues a dark elven mate, fixated on aesthetics over personality, ability or culture. Very shameful.
Used in sunlight hours like ‘good day’, with less cheerful connotations.
Highly derogatory label for a Kharajyr, implying they are feral and cut off from their fallen empire and dead goddess; the proper term is ‘velubol’.
An elf of at least half dark elf descent crossed with another subrace, not deemed worthy of ‘maehr’. Meant respectfully but can be controversial.
A person with long uncut hair, often from piety; respectful to religious clans, but an insult implying fragility to martial bands.
A blessing for others.
A blessing for a personal group.
Reserved for the morning: a neutral greeting and an observation that dawn has come. Literally ‘little sun’.
Title for the maehr considered the high venure of the nation at the time.
An informal greeting, more intimate than ‘vraz’; derived from ancient elven ‘good evening’ but used at any time.
Best translated ‘Drow’: umbrella term for dark elves and mori’quessir, sometimes dark dwarves. Some use it over malyker to leave out the ‘elf’.
Derogatory: fusion of labek ‘white’ and leytura ‘rose’, for heartlander and highlander humans, especially zealous canonists.
Affectionate word for someone silly, playful or goofy; not an insult.
A challenge.
A call to arms.
‘Let’s go [together]’. Literally ‘we go’.
How many dark elves self-identify; a less literal label for ‘proper’ dark elves (all maehr are malyker, not all malyker are maehr). ‘maly’ elf and ‘ker’ dark are loaned from ancient elven.
Insult for a once-maehr who accepted a bashkymyr’s advances; strips the title of maehr.
The current matriarch or sometimes patriarch of a Tribe, Clan or House.
Conservative expression of matriarchal values for a male maehr who strives beyond his station: boisterous, arrogant or free-spirited. Literally ‘unmanlike’.
An exalted elder who was once High Priestess/Priest and advises the current one.
‘come here’. ‘Ska’at’ alone means ‘come’.
Refusal/dismissal of a challenge; also used to defuse one or to recognise peace. Literally ‘the tide sleeps’.
Interpreted as ‘be well’ and ‘well met’; a greeting or farewell.
‘Go’, as a dismissal.
A dismissal, ‘go in shame’. ‘Bashuk’ (honour, from mori’quessir) is a hurtful term.
A fond farewell blessing, ‘go with the moon’.
Title for the husband of the Primarch; an elevated ‘patriarch’.
Sir / Ma’am / gender-neutral form. A respectful address, not a knightly styling.
A corruption of ancient elven ‘farewell’.
‘Lunar’; a full moon cycle, used with numbers for months (OOC days), e.g. az-velel = one month.
‘High lunar’: seven moon cycles, used with numbers for years (OOC weeks), e.g. az-velelana = one year.
Issuing a formal challenge (duel, contest, dispute). Literally ‘the moon calls/pulls’.
Ceremonious greeting for superiors, with a salute or bow; also a holy word from teachers to disciples.
Formal greeting exclusive to dark elves, for respect or familial love; taboo for non-dark elves.
An informal greeting, ‘hi’ or ‘hello’. Literally ‘good’.
Title for the wife of the Primarch; an elevated ‘matriarch’.
Sacred: the moon visible in daylight, ‘pale day’ (written with holy x’s, from zabyth + ezan); also days of religious observation.
Sacred: the moon setting over the ocean, ‘pale tide’; seen as an omen or blessing (from zabyth + thet’uzh).
A sincere thanks for significant gifts or favours. Literally ‘bless yourself after’.
Closest word to ‘please?’, but it means begging and is humiliating; very insulting to a maehr. Loaned from mori’quessir ‘joros’ (to ask).
A tenacious warrior fighting for own passions and pragmatism; also mercenary, bandit, assassin when a dark elf. Neutral.
A righteous warrior pledged to an ideal; also city guard, paladin or templar when a dark elf. Neutral.
Accepting a challenge. Literally ‘the ocean pushes!’ / ‘the sea answers!’.
Very derogatory, ‘mud ear’: an elf or part-elf with no culture or who emulates heartlander or highlander cultures; like ‘mongrel’.
